newsitem.title: USA: U.S. extends halt on aid to Cambodia government.
newsitem.headline: U.S. extends halt on aid to Cambodia government.

text.p: The United States said on Friday it was extending indefinitely its suspension of aid to the Cambodian government but help going directly to the Cambodian people would continue.

State Department spokesman James Rubin also said U.S. embassy employees and dependents evacuated after fighting in Phnom Penh last month were being allowed to return to Phnom Penh because the situation there was now safer.

The United States suspended its aid programme to Cambodia for 30 days after the bloody July 6 coup in which Hun Sen ousted his former coalition partner and co-prime minister, Prince Norodom Ranariddh.

"The Secretary (of State) has decided today to extend indefinitely the suspension of assistance to Cambodia until progress towards free and fair elections has been made," Rubin told a regular news conference. Elections are planned for May next year.

"During this suspension period our estimate is roughly two thirds of the assistance that had been...planned will be suspended because that assistance would go one way or another to the government of Cambodia...," Rubin said. But he said about $20 million dollars would still be available for humanitarian needs.

"We are sending back our embassy employees and their dependents because we have decided that Phnom Penh is now safe enough to permit their return," he said. He said the U.S. ambassador in Phnom Penh had reported that "the city is now as safe as it was before the fighting."
